name: DAX
description: Germany's DAX rose 0.34%, extending a modest advance. It matters as a read on European exporters, manufacturers, banks, and demand across a major U.S. trading partner.
licensing_note: Exchange index data are proprietary; linked exchange and market sources retained.

name: Nikkei 225
description: Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 1.05%. Its technology and export exposure can connect the index with chip demand, the yen, and Asian manufacturing.
licensing_note: Nikkei index data are copyrighted; citation and linked source retained.

name: KOSPI
description: South Korea's KOSPI fell 0.89% after touching a higher intraday level. Its semiconductor and export concentration offers an early read on chip demand and global manufacturing.
data_provider: Korea Exchange via KB Financial Group
licensing_note: Korea Exchange index data are proprietary; linked exchange and issuer sources retained.

name: Nasdaq Composite
description: The technology-heavy Nasdaq rose 1.19%, reflecting renewed demand for growth shares. Its sensitivity to rates and AI spending makes it a useful gauge of investor risk appetite.
licensing_note: FRED republishes the Nasdaq series; citation and linked source retained.

name: Dow Jones Industrial Average
description: The Dow edged up 0.18%, showing a quieter move among 30 established companies. It helps reveal whether market gains extend beyond technology into industrial, financial, and consumer businesses.
data_provider: S&P Dow Jones Indices via FRED
licensing_note: Index data are proprietary; citation and linked FRED source retained.

name: Russell 2000
description: The Russell 2000 rose 0.50%, continuing a three-session advance. Its smaller US companies are more exposed to domestic borrowing costs, wages, and consumer demand than multinational giants.
data_provider: FTSE Russell level reported by The Associated Press
licensing_note: FTSE Russell index data are proprietary; the reporting and index methodology links are retained.

name: 2-year Treasury yield
description: The two-year Treasury yield rose 0.05 percentage points. Markets use it to compare near-term borrowing costs with Federal Reserve policy settings.
licensing_note: Federal Reserve public data; FRED citation retained.

name: 10-year minus 2-year yield spread
description: The yield-curve spread widened as long rates moved further above short rates. Banks, borrowers, and economists watch its shape for clues about credit conditions and growth expectations.
data_provider: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
licensing_note: Calculated from Treasury public data; FRED citation retained.

name: 30-year fixed mortgage rate
description: The average mortgage rate rose 0.25 percentage points to 7.28%. Higher financing costs reduce home affordability, monthly purchasing power, and demand across housing-related businesses.
licensing_note: Copyright Freddie Mac; reprinted by FRED with permission and citation.

name: Euro to dollar
description: The euro gained 0.24% against the dollar. The pair connects two major trading blocs, affecting European travel, imported goods, and the translated revenue of multinational companies.
licensing_note: Federal Reserve public exchange-rate data; FRED citation retained.

name: Dollar to yen
description: The dollar gained 0.11% against the yen. The pair can connect U.S.-Japan rate differences with cars, electronics, overseas earnings, and global funding trades.
licensing_note: Federal Reserve public exchange-rate data; FRED citation retained.

name: Pound to dollar
description: The pound rose 0.29% against the dollar. Sterling links major financial centers, so its direction can affect UK travel, British holdings, and US companies earning pounds.
licensing_note: Federal Reserve public exchange-rate data; FRED citation retained.

name: WTI crude oil
description: West Texas Intermediate crude fell 3.23%. As the U.S. oil benchmark, sustained moves can reach gasoline, freight, plastics, airline costs, inflation expectations, and energy-company profits.
data_provider: U.S. Energy Information Administration via FRED
licensing_note: U.S. government source series; FRED citation retained.

name: Natural gas
description: Henry Hub natural gas rose 1.60%, lifting the U.S. wholesale benchmark. It matters for household heating, electricity prices, fertilizer production, factories, and liquefied-natural-gas exporters.
data_provider: U.S. Energy Information Administration via FRED
licensing_note: U.S. government source series; FRED citation retained.

name: Copper
description: Copper slipped 0.07%, leaving the industrial metal near recent levels. Construction, power grids, vehicles, and electronics make it useful for reading global demand and future project costs.
licensing_note: IMF benchmark data reprinted by FRED with citation and terms retained.
